title: Autism Applications
subtitle: Avoid normalisation narratives and overclaiming
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating autism applications within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain autism applications without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in autism applications.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to autism applications.

sections.explainSimply: Some autistic people use neurofeedback with goals such as attention, sleep or self-regulation.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Autism is not a unitary brain-wave abnormality. Goals should be person-centred and avoid framing neurodivergence itself as damage to be normalised.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: A 2025 systematic review found signals of cognitive benefit across a small, heterogeneous literature, but the evidence base remains too limited and methodologically variable to infer efficacy for autism as a condition. Define person-centred functional targets, monitor sensory load and assent, and avoid normalisation goals.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Testing a treatment hypothesis: improvement must be meaningful, measured and compared with plausible alternatives.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand autism applications to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Do not promise to “treat autism” or erase identity-linked traits.
sections.clinicalPearl: Measure benefit and harm with the same seriousness.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using autism applications predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Do not promise to “treat autism” or erase identity-linked traits. Evidence classification: preliminary and heterogeneous; selected cognitive outcomes are not evidence that autism itself is normalised or cured.

mechanismMap.detail: Evidence is heterogeneous and often limited by small samples, non-blinded outcomes and variable protocols. Monitor sensory load and assent.

mechanismMap.detail: Test whether learned regulation changes meaningful behaviour or symptoms outside training.
